chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who passes by date palms, grain ears, and fruit, and whether it is permissible for him to eat from them without the owner's permission, whether out of necessity or not. He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fruit or grain from a field without the owner's permission?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on selling fruits, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that casual consumption of produce like dates and grain is permissible without the owner's explicit consent, regardless of whether it is driven by necessity or mere convenience. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *istihlak* (consumption) and highlights the flexibility in property rights regarding agricultural goods, distinguishing between significant appropriation and minor, non-damaging use. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the boundaries of private ownership versus communal or casual access in Islamic commercial law.
